options: A query built as a string at runtime, then executed
A query that automatically optimizes itself
A query that only works with dynamic data types
A synonym for a stored procedure
questions.explain: Unlike static queries written out in full in advance, dynamic SQL is assembled as text and then run.

questions.q: Why can't a normal parameter always handle what dynamic SQL is used for?
options: Parameters can only hold numeric values
Parameters only substitute values, never table or column names/identifiers
Parameters are deprecated in modern T-SQL
Parameters cannot be used inside stored procedures
questions.explain: When the table name, column name, or sort column itself needs to vary, a normal parameter can't do that job.

questions.q: Why is directly string-concatenating untrusted input into a SQL string dangerous?
options: It always causes a syntax error
It makes the query run slower, but is otherwise safe
It only affects performance, not security
It creates a SQL injection vulnerability — malicious text can be smuggled in and executed as part of the query
questions.explain: The example shows how something like '; DROP TABLE Production.Product; --' could be injected via unsafe concatenation.

questions.q: How does sp_executesql avoid the SQL injection risk?
options: It takes parameters separately from the query string, so SQL Server treats the values strictly as data, never as executable SQL
It refuses to run any query containing user input
It only works with numeric parameters, eliminating the risk
It automatically escapes every single quote in the input
questions.explain: This is the core safety mechanism — proper parameterization, not string concatenation.

questions.q: What are the three things passed to sp_executesql?
options: The table name, column name, and WHERE clause separately
A stored procedure name and its parameters
Only the query string and nothing else
The query string, a declaration of expected parameters (as a string), and the actual parameter values
questions.explain: EXEC sp_executesql @SQL, N'@Color NVARCHAR(50)', @Color = @ColorInput; shows all three pieces.
